findings.violation: A fixed width of 960px forces horizontal scrolling once the viewport narrows to 320px, with no responsive override.
findings.fix: Cap the element's width with a relative max-width (a percentage or viewport unit), or add a media query that shrinks it below 320px.

line 20,

element, text 'Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk. Updates p...'
findings.evidence: text color #999999 on background #ffffff, contrast ratio 2.85:1
findings.violation: Contrast ratio 2.85:1 is below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text.
findings.fix: Darken the text or lighten the background until the ratio reaches at least 4.5:1.

findings.violation: The viewport meta tag sets user-scalable=no, disabling browser zoom entirely.
findings.fix: Remove user-scalable=no so readers can zoom the page.

findings.location: line 11, <nav> element, the page's header navigation
findings.evidence: <nav id="nav"> contains only two links, "Accessibility" and "Fares and passes"; no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere else in the document
findings.violation: The page offers exactly one mechanism for a reader to locate it within the site, the primary navigation menu, with no site search, sitemap, or breadcrumb trail present, and the page is not one step in a linear process that would exempt it.
findings.fix: Add a second, genuinely independent wayfinding mechanism, such as a breadcrumb trail or a site search, rather than relying on the navigation menu alone.

findings.evidence: heading text 'Accessibility improvements' over a section whose only content reads 'Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day.' and 'Local residents may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day.'
findings.violation: The heading's wording names a topic, accessibility improvements, that neither paragraph nor the image alt text in this section addresses; the section's actual content is schedule and fare-adjustment information, so a reader scanning headings for accessibility content is misled into skipping past it and finding nothing here instead.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to describe the section's actual content, for example 'Schedule and fare updates', or move content describing accessibility improvements into this section.

findings.evidence: heading text 'Weekend service' over a section covering fare adjustments, a service status card, a three-step plan and payment wizard, and a route and contact form, with no content specific to weekend service
findings.violation: The heading's wording names a topic, weekend service, that no content in this section addresses; the section instead covers fare adjustments, a status card, a plan and payment wizard, and an unrelated form, so a reader scanning headings for weekend-service information finds nothing here that matches.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to describe the section's actual content, or split this section by topic so each heading matches what follows it.

findings.evidence: boundary color #9d9d9d against adjacent background #ffffff, contrast ratio 2.71:1
findings.violation: Component boundary contrast ratio 2.71:1 is below the 3:1 AA minimum.
findings.fix: Darken the border or outline color, or change the adjacent background, until the ratio reaches at least 3:1.

findings.violation: A fixed height combined with clipped overflow truncates this element's text once a reader applies wider line, paragraph, letter, or word spacing.
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height so the element grows with its content, or replace the clipped overflow with visible or auto.

findings.violation: No label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title identifies what this control expects.
findings.fix: Add a <label for> pointing at this control's id, wrap the control in a <label>, or set aria-label.
